title: Your child has a fever: what to do at home, and when to go to the hospital
intro: Your child feels hot at 2 am. What should you do?

In this calm, simple guide, a paediatrician explains how to check a fever properly, how to care for your child at home, the common mistakes parents make, and the red-flag signs that mean you should see a doctor straight away.
chapters: Your child feels hot at 2 am
Red flags: when to see a doctor
points: What temperature counts as a fever (38 °C / 100.4 °F)
How to measure it the right way (digital thermometer, armpit)
Home care: fluids, light clothes, rest, and medicine dosed by weight
5 mistakes to avoid: ice-cold sponging, wrapping up, aspirin, extra doses, antibiotics at home
Red flags: baby under 3 months, very sleepy or floppy, breathing difficulty, a rash that doesn't fade, fits, dehydration, fever over 5 days
